** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Register the test driver once per process.** `sql.Register` panics on a duplicate driver name. `TestQuerySQLAppliesTimeout` calls it on every run. `go test -count=2` runs the test twice in one process, so the second run panics. Move the registration to a package-level `init` function so it runs once per process.
Suggested fix

```diff --- "a/checks/sql_timeout_test.go" +++ "b/checks/sql_timeout_test.go" @@ -26,8 +26,11 @@ return nil, ctx.Err() } -func TestQuerySQLAppliesTimeout(t *testing.T) { - sql.Register("blocking-test", blockingDriver{}) +func init() { + sql.Register("blocking-test", blockingDriver{}) +} + +func TestQuerySQLAppliesTimeout(t *testing.T) { check := &v1.SQLCheck{Timeout: 1} timeout := check.GetQueryTimeout() ```

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the actual change: querySQL no longer multiplies the configured timeout by time.Second, so the SQL query timeout is applied in seconds as configured. The raw summary confirms the one-line change to checks/sql.go and a new test, TestQuerySQLAppliesTimeout, that checks the timeout. The title is specific and matches the main change.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#2305` requires SQL checks to have a timeout and to cancel queries after that timeout. At the reviewed head, `CheckSQL` passes `check.GetQueryTimeout()` to `querySQL`, whose parameter `timout` is a `time.Duration`. The PR changes `ctx.WithTimeout(timout * time.Second)` to `ctx.WithTimeout(timout)` in `checks/sql.go`. The base code multiplied a duration by `time.Second` again, so the deadline was too long to enforce the configured timeout. With the fix, `db.QueryContext(tctx, query)` receives the configured deadline and cancels the query when it expires. The new test `TestQuerySQLAppliesTimeout` (`checks/sql_timeout_test.go`) uses a fake driver whose `QueryContext` blocks on `ctx.Done()`, and it asserts that `querySQL` returns an error within 5 seconds with `Timeout: 1`. The author reports that the test fails on master and passes with the fix. I did not run the test. The unit of `GetQueryTimeout()` is inferred from the parameter type and the PR description, not from the `api/v1` source, which I could not locate.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff (merge base 47fd165 to head 98e717f) has two files. `checks/sql.go` changes one line, which removes the extra `time.Second` multiplication that causes the timeout bug. `checks/sql_timeout_test.go` adds a test for that behavior and registers a test-only `database/sql` driver. Both changes support issue `#2305`. No unrelated changes appear in the diff.
